questions.question_text: The first hydrolytic product of STREPTOMYCIN with methanolic hydrochloric acid is given below. Identify the correct one.

options.D: Streptamine + Streptose dimethyl acetal + N-methyl glucosamine

questions.explanation: Hydrolysis of streptomycin with methanolic HCl yields streptidine and methyl strepto-biosaminide dimethyl acetal.

questions.question_text: One of the following drugs interferes with cellular metabolism, especially the synthesis of Mycolic acid. Identify.
questions.explanation: Isonicotinic acid hydrazide (Isoniazid) inhibits mycolic acid synthesis in mycobacteria.

questions.question_text: A synthetic sweetening agent which is approximately 200 times sweeter than sucrose and has no after taste is:
questions.explanation: Aspartame is approximately 200 times sweeter than sucrose and lacks the bitter aftertaste often associated with saccharin.

questions.question_text: In capsules ROTOSORT is used for
questions.explanation: Rotosort is a machine specifically used for inspecting and sorting filled capsules.

questions.question_text: Shellac is used for the purpose of coating of tablets as
questions.explanation: Shellac is a traditional natural polymer used primarily as an enteric coating agent for tablets.

questions.question_text: Listed below are structures of some drugs. One of them prevents the incorporation of PABA into folic acid. Identify: (a) c1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)NC2=NC(=CS2)C (b) COC1=C(C(=C2C(=C1)OC)N=C(N2)N)OC (c) NC1=NC2=C(N1)N=CN2[C@@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]O3)CO)O (d) ClC1=CC=C(C=C1)NC(=O)NC2=CC=CC=C2
questions.explanation: Structure A represents a sulfonamide derivative (Sulfamethoxazole), which competitively inhibits dihydropterate synthase by mimicking PABA.

questions.question_text: In Quantitative T.L.C. radioactive material can be studied by
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials on TLC plates are quantified using radiation detectors such as a Geiger counter or scintillation counters.

questions.question_text: One of the following ingredients which improves the flow property of granules is:
questions.explanation: Glidants are added to powder formulations to improve flow properties by reducing interparticle friction.

questions.question_text: The wavelength source in N.M.R. spectrometer is
questions.explanation: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy utilizes radiofrequency radiation generated by an RF oscillator.

questions.question_text: One of the following materials is used for the preparation of master grating. Identify
questions.explanation: Master diffraction gratings are typically ruled on aluminum-coated surfaces or blanks due to its reflective properties and ductility.

questions.question_text: Benzathine penicillin is

options.A: An equimolecular composition of Amoxicillin + N.N dibenzyl ethylene diamine
options.B: A molecular complexation of Benzyl penicillin+ N.N dibenzyl ethylene diamine
options.C: A molecular complexation of Cloxacillin + ethylene diamine
options.D: Equimolecular proportion of Amoxicillin + ethylene diamine

questions.explanation: Benzathine penicillin G is formed by the salt formation/complexation of benzyl penicillin with N,N'-dibenzylethylenediamine.

questions.question_text: Schick test is performed to ascertain susceptibility to
questions.explanation: The Schick test is a clinical skin test used to determine whether a person is susceptible to diphtheria.

questions.question_text: Which of the following commonly available large volume dextrose solution for intravenous use is isotonic?
questions.explanation: A $5\% \text{ w/v}$ dextrose solution in water is considered isotonic with human body fluids.

questions.question_text: The term bioavailability refers to the

options.A: Relationship between the physical and chemical properties of a drug and the systemic absorption of the drug
options.B: Measurement of the rate and amount of therapeutically active drug that reaches the systemic circulation
options.C: Movement of drug into the body tissues over time
options.D: Dissolution of a drug in the gastrointestinal tract

questions.explanation: Bioavailability is defined as the rate and extent to which the active ingredient is absorbed from a drug product and becomes available at the site of action.

questions.question_text: Among the propellants used in aerosols one of the following is used for topical pharmaceutical aerosols.
questions.explanation: Trichloromonofluoromethane (Propellant 11) and Dichlorodifluoromethane (Propellant 12) are standard chlorofluorocarbon propellants historically used in aerosols.

questions.question_text: The principal structural component of the cell wall in bacteria is made up of
questions.explanation: Bacterial cell walls are primarily composed of peptidoglycan (murein), a polymer consisting of sugars and amino acids.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has the highest degree of ionization in an aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: A lower $\text{pK}_a$ value for a weak acid indicates a stronger acid, which ionizes to a greater extent at a given pH.

questions.question_text: Tetracyclines are avoided during pregnancy because

options.B: It may affect the bone growth of foetus
options.C: It causes discolouration of mothers teeth

questions.explanation: Tetracyclines bind to calcium in developing teeth and bones, leading to dental staining and inhibition of bone growth in the fetus.

questions.question_text: The Xenobiotics that does not cause nephrotoxicity is
questions.explanation: Isoniazid is primarily metabolized by the liver (acetylation) and is not typically associated with direct nephrotoxicity like cisplatin, aminoglycosides, or streptozocin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following function of OPIOID receptors?
questions.explanation: Opioid receptor activation inhibits presynaptic calcium channels and opens potassium channels, leading to a decrease in the release of neurotransmitters such as norepinephrine.

questions.question_text: Assume that a typical type of Cancer is susceptible to an individual drug. Listed below are some therapeutic combination of anti-cancer drugs which are rationale except one. Identify.
questions.explanation: Chlorambucil and Melphalan are both alkylating agents with similar mechanisms and overlapping toxicities, making their combination irrational.

questions.question_text: One of the following emissions from the decay of Radio nuclides is commonly used in sterilization. Identify
questions.explanation: Gamma rays (typically from Cobalt-60) have high penetration power and are widely used for industrial radiation sterilization.

questions.question_text: Clinically available anticancer agents have one of the underlying mechanism of action, they act by

options.C: Receptor site blockade of cancer cell content

questions.explanation: Anticancer agents function primarily by inhibiting cell growth, proliferation, and inducing apoptosis in rapidly dividing cells.

questions.question_text: Listed below are some of the common Radio nuclides used in Nuclear Pharmacy which one is generator produced?
questions.explanation: Technetium-99m ($^{99m}\text{Tc}$) is obtained commercially using a Molybdenum-99/Technetium-99m generator.

questions.question_text: Smallpox Vaccine contains
questions.explanation: The smallpox vaccine contains live vaccinia virus, which is closely related to the smallpox virus.

questions.question_text: The solution strength of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in terms of $\text{mg/L}$ for a Calcium injection which contains $5\text{ mEq. Calcium}$ ($\text{Ca}^{++}$) per $100\text{ ml}$ is given below. Identify the correct one. [At $40\text{ wt} - \text{Ca}^{++} = 40$].
questions.explanation: Calculation: $5\text{ mEq/100 mL} = 50\text{ mEq/L}$. Equivalent weight of $\text{Ca}^{++} = 40 / 2 = 20\text{ g/Eq} = 20\text{ mg/mEq}$. $\text{Concentration} = 50\text{ mEq/L} \times 20\text{ mg/mEq} = 1000\text{ mg/L}$.

questions.question_text: Listed below are some of the drug intermediates. Choose the correct one for the synthesis of Procainamide.

options.A: p-nitro benzyl chloride and Diethyl amino ethylamine
options.B: p-nitro benzyl chloride and ethyl amino ethylamine
options.C: p-nitro cinnamoyl chloride and Diethyl amino ethylamine
options.D: p-nitro benzene and Diethyl amino ethylamine

questions.explanation: Procainamide is synthesized by reacting p-nitrobenzoyl chloride with diethylaminoethylamine, followed by reduction of the nitro group.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct name for Digitoxigenin.
questions.explanation: Digitoxigenin is a cardenolide steroid aglycone possessing two hydroxyl groups at the $3\beta$ and $14\beta$ positions.

questions.question_text: 2, 6-dimethyl aniline and chloro acetyl chloride are the starting compounds for the synthesis of one of the following drugs. Choose the correct one.
questions.explanation: Lidocaine is synthesized by the reaction of 2,6-dimethylaniline with chloroacetyl chloride, followed by diethylamine displacement.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct geneva name for TRANYL CYPROMINE.
questions.explanation: Tranylcypromine is marketed as a racemic mixture of trans-2-phenylcyclopropylamine.

questions.question_text: In take of which of the following should be avoided by a patient taking on oral anticoagulant?
questions.explanation: Menadione (Vitamin K3) promotes blood clotting and antagonizes the effects of oral anticoagulants like warfarin.

questions.question_text: Ellipsoidal schizolysigenous oil glands are important diagnostic of
questions.explanation: Clove flower buds exhibit characteristic ellipsoidal schizolysigenous oil glands under microscopic examination.

questions.question_text: Catecholamines act by

options.A: Decrease the amount of glucose released into the blood
options.B: Increase the utilization of glucose by muscle
options.C: Increase the amount of glucose released into the blood
options.D: Decrease the amount of glucose in the muscle.

questions.explanation: Catecholamines (such as epinephrine) stimulate glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, increasing blood glucose levels.

questions.question_text: Hyoscyamine an alkaloid obtained from Atropa belladonna

options.A: Readily racemises to atropine with ethanolic alkali. Atropine is (\pm) Hyoscyamine
options.B: Readily disintegrates into atropine with acid solution. Atropine is (-) Hyoscyamine
options.C: Readily rearranges into atropine with acid solution. Atropine is (+) Hyoscyamine
options.D: Readily racemise to atropine with ethanolic alkali. Atropine is (+)...

questions.explanation: Hyoscyamine is the levorotatory isomer, and treatment with dilute alkali readily racemizes it into racemic DL-hyoscyamine, known as atropine.

questions.question_text: Identify the correct molecule which controls the biosynthesis of proteins in living organisms
questions.explanation: DNA stores the master genetic code which ultimately controls protein biosynthesis via transcription and translation.
